prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1311; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officer's narrative: On arrival at the intersection in Pearland, Texas, I found two vehicles stopped at an angle to one another. Driver 1 stated that while turning left across the lane of oncoming traffic, the vehicle was struck on the front driver-side area by Driver 2, who was proceeding straight. Driver 2 gave the same account and said the collision occurred just as described by Driver 1. Two independent witnesses on the sidewalk told me they saw the impact and that the left turn was made in front of the approaching car. Scene photographs taken at my direction show the damage pattern consistent with those statements. Driver 1 reported pain in the left knee and was evaluated at the scene; the type of injury is consistent with a force of this kind striking the driver's lower body against the interior. A passenger was also seated in the front right seat and confirmed to me that they were in the vehicle at the time. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy for the vehicle involved. Driver 1 reported no prior damage to the vehicle. Some of the body damage visible on the rear quarter panel may not have resulted from this impact and was not assessed further at the scene. Both drivers were cooperative, and no citations were issued at the time of this report.
